text:
maria: quick sync — customer asks for hardened on-prem runtime: FIPS build + customer HSM. Need: minimal RBAC for kms shim, netpol pattern to keep deny-by-default, conntrack / sysctl guidance, and where to stash HSM incident runbook.

devin: short answer: per-namespace ServiceAccount with narrowly scoped Role/RoleBinding. Do NOT use cluster-admin or write broad secrets. Map runtime SA to customer HSM role with only Encrypt/Decrypt and optional Sign.

ash: add: if you need attestation, include Sign. Many customers use a local shim agent (sidecar or daemonset) — prefer unix domain socket to avoid extra conntrack pressure.

maria: unix socket is preferred, but some legacy HSM shims only speak TCP on host. How to keep network locked down in that case?

sre-jordan: pattern we've used: create a dedicated namespace "kms-agent" (or label nodes) and run the agent there. In customer-runtime namespace use a NetworkPolicy with Egress only to pods with label app=kms-proxy in that namespace. Default deny egress for everything else. If agent uses hostNetwork, scope egress to the node CIDR range, not 0.0.0.0/0.

devin: watch conntrack in rootless containers. Short-lived ephemeral connections can blow up nf_conntrack. Recommend either UDS or keep a long-lived pooled connection. Also recommend bumping net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max.

ash: concrete sysctl guidance: add to onboarding: net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=131072 and net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_buckets=32768 as conservative starting point for medium/high throughput. Note: customers on older kernels may need distro-specific tuning.

maria: audit logs — customer wants KMS events to SIEM. What do we log? resource IDs? plaintext?

sre-jordan: log structured JSON events: event_type, principal, resource_id (hashed or masked), action, outcome, timestamp. NEVER log keys or plaintext ciphertext. For FIPS customers use SHA2-256 for hashing and annotate algorithm in the event.

sec-bot: CI note: any change to kms client or default RBAC must go through the kms-client risk review. https://redwood.internal/policies/kms-client-change :lock:

devin: incident behavior: fail-closed for new decrypts (return 503) but allow serving of cached non-sensitive content. Emit metric kms.decrypt.errors and increase severity on consecutive failures > 5m. Pager: infra-oncall then security if integrity risk.

ops-liz: where to keep HSM operator runbook? Propose private repo ops/runbooks/hsm-fallback.md with playbook: detect -> fail-closed -> alert customer HSM ops -> rotate ephemeral keys if needed -> rollback feature flag. Link that from onboarding docs.

ash: vuln triage update: we discovered CVE in libenvelope v2.1.3 affecting IV handling. Patch plan: upgrade to v2.1.4, add short-lived feature flag to enable software envelope fallback, and an emergency image push for Private/Dedicated customers. Schedule rollout window and notify affected customers.

maria: can we drop short RBAC + NetworkPolicy snippets for the onboarding page? I'd like copy-paste examples.

sre-jordan: dropping minimal examples — paste into docs and tweak ports/labels per customer.

```yaml
# Role + RoleBinding (namespace-scoped, least privilege)
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: runtime-kms-role
  namespace: customer-runtime
rules:
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["secrets"]
  verbs: ["get"]
# If runtime needs to list services/endpoints for discovery, scope that specifically
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: runtime-kms-binding
  namespace: customer-runtime
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: runtime-sa
  namespace: customer-runtime
roleRef:
  kind: Role
  name: runtime-kms-role
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
```

```yaml
# NetworkPolicy: allow only egress to kms-proxy in kms-agent namespace
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-egress-to-kms-proxy
  namespace: customer-runtime
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: runtime
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          role: kms-agent-namespace
      podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: kms-proxy
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 1812
```

maria: nice. two final asks: 1) test plan for conntrack under rootless, 2) short wording for onboarding about feature flag and emergency rollback.

devin: 1) test plan: run a synthetic load that opens+closes 10k short-lived TCP connections per minute from rootless runtime to agent, watch /proc/net/nf_conntrack and conntrack counters, and validate metrics & alerts trigger. I'd like a test cluster to run this. 2) onboarding blurb: "If HSM-related vuln/incident occurs we ship an emergency image with software-fallback behind a feature flag. Customers can opt-in temporarily while their HSM is remediated. Contact support for assisted rollout."

ops-liz: I'll create ops/runbooks/hsm-fallback.md and a PR for onboarding with the RBAC/netpol snippets and sysctl recommendations.

maria: thanks all. ping me if you want test clusters — happy to coordinate load runs. :raised_hands:
